faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before you start your trial.
faq.howItWorksQuestion: How does downDATA check my services?
faq.howItWorksAnswer: We poll each tracked service's public status page as often as every 30 seconds and update your dashboard the moment anything changes.
faq.trialQuestion: What happens after my 14-day trial ends?
faq.trialAnswer: You get full access for 14 days with no card required. When the trial ends, pick the plan that fits. Nothing is charged automatically.
faq.cancelQuestion: Can I change or cancel my plan anytime?
faq.cancelAnswer: Yes. Upgrade, downgrade, or cancel whenever you like. There's no lock-in or long-term contract.
faq.notificationsQuestion: Will my team get notified when something breaks?
faq.notificationsAnswer: Connect Slack in a few clicks and incidents post straight to your channel. Every plan includes unlimited team seats, so the whole team stays in the loop.
faq.monitorCountAnswer: Each service you track (GitHub, Supabase, Cloudflare, or anything else on Atlassian Statuspage) counts as one monitor against your plan's limit.
faq.emailSmsQuestion: Can I get notified by email or SMS too, not just Slack?
faq.emailSmsAnswer: Yes, connect one or more email addresses or phone numbers alongside Slack. SMS lets you pick which severities are worth a text, from critical-only up to everything.
faq.boardsQuestion: Can I organize monitors for different teams?
faq.boardsAnswer: Yes, group your tracked services into boards, so each team only sees the services that matter to them.
faq.scopeQuestion: Does downDATA monitor my own servers, or just public status pages?
faq.scopeAnswer: Just public status pages. downDATA tracks services built on Atlassian Statuspage, like GitHub, Supabase, and Cloudflare. It's not a tool for pinging or monitoring your own infrastructure.

about.title: About <brand>down</brand>DATA
about.storyBody: <brand>down</brand>DATA started in August 2026, built by one developer annoyed that checking whether the tools your app depends on are having a bad day required either babysitting five different status pages or paying a service like StatusGator hundreds of dollars a month for something that's fundamentally just polling a public API. <brand>down</brand>DATA does the same job — tracking GitHub, Supabase, Cloudflare, and anything else on Atlassian Statuspage — for a fraction of the price.
about.teamBody: <brand>down</brand>DATA is built and maintained by Lukáš Bujdoš, a web developer based in Slovakia <flag/>, currently as a solo project. It's new — actively built in the open, one feature at a time — rather than a company with a headcount to pad out an About page.

support.title: Support
support.subtitle: Need a hand? Here's the fastest way to reach us.
support.chatBody: Chat with us right in the app — we typically reply within a few hours.
support.emailBody: Prefer email? Write to us and we'll get back to you.
support.faqBody: Common questions about how downDATA works are already answered there.

features.monitors: Track the live status of any service on Atlassian Statuspage (GitHub, Supabase, Cloudflare, and anything else your team depends on), checked as often as every 30 seconds.
features.incidents: A unified timeline of incidents across every service you track, so you don't have to check five different status pages to know what's actually going on.
features.maintenances: Scheduled and in-progress maintenance windows across all your tracked services, in one place. Planned downtime never looks like an outage.
features.integrations: Connect Slack and send status updates straight to a channel your team already watches, so no one has to remember to check a dashboard.
features.slack: Post new incidents and status updates straight to a Slack channel your team already watches. Connect it in a couple of clicks, no bot to configure.
features.email: Get incident and status updates delivered straight to an email distribution list. Connect one or more addresses and everyone stays in the loop, no login required.
features.sms: Get a text the moment something major or critical breaks. Add one or more numbers and choose which severities are worth a text, from critical-only up to everything.
features.history: Pick any tracked service and see its incident history over the last 12 months, useful the next time someone asks whether this has happened before.
features.boards: Group your tracked services into boards for different teams, so everyone sees only the services that matter to them.
features.statusPages: Publish a public, read-only status page for any board's tracked services, so your customers can check for themselves before they open a ticket.
